references.text: The immediate context that establishes the rules for priests' ritual impurity due to death and specifies which close relatives are exempt from the prohibition.
General laws concerning ritual impurity through contact with dead bodies that apply to all Israelites, forming the basis for the stricter rules for priests.
Ezekiel's repetition of the laws regarding priests' ritual impurity due to death in the future temple system, with similar restrictions.
The even stricter rules for the high priest, who may not become ritually unclean even for his closest relatives so as not to profane the sanctuary.
Aaron and his sons were forbidden to mourn Nadab and Abihu in the usual way, illustrating the principle that priestly service takes precedence over personal grief.
